tools.reason: The entry point: every zone-scoped tool needs a zone_id, and this is the only way to discover one. Also what the legacy cloudflare status verb reads.
Adding a domain to the account. Additive and reversible by zones_delete; the plan and subscription are a separate call.
One zone in full: status, name servers, plan, paused flag. Reads the state every other zone tool acts on.
The settable zone fields (paused, plan, type, vanity name servers). Pausing a zone takes the site off Cloudflare at once.
Deleting the zone stops DNS from answering and mail from arriving: nothing is served until the domain is added back and its records are rebuilt.
Re-runs the zone activation check, which is the step that finishes a migration after the registrar's name servers point at Cloudflare.
Reads whether the zone is held and until when. A hold is what keeps a zone from being deleted or moved by mistake mid-migration.
Binds a hold to the zone for a number of days, the safety net for a cutover.
Extends or shortens an existing hold, the operation a long migration needs.
Releases the hold, which also re-enables the account-transfer path it was blocking. Reviewed as a normal gated write: it protects nothing by itself.
Lists a zone's records with the API's own filters (name, type, tag, comment, content). The read half of the legacy dns-list verb.
Creates one record. The spec's body is a union of per-record-type schemas and the resolver flattens it to the 11 fields they share.
Reads one record by id, the lookup a caller needs before an update it does not want to guess at.
Changes the fields it is given and leaves the rest alone, which is what an upsert during a cutover wants.
Replaces the whole record: a field left out is cleared. Distinct from update on purpose, so a caller picks which semantics they mean.
Removing a record takes that name off the air until it is created again; the service it pointed at is unreachable meanwhile.
One call that posts, puts, patches and deletes a set of records at once. It is the tool that can take several names off the air in a single request.
The zone's DNS-level settings in one read: zone transfer, flattening, multi-provider, nameserver behaviour.
Writes those settings. It is a PATCH because the API accepts the subset it is given; the schema carries the 9 documented fields.
Reads whether DNSSEC is on for the zone and the DS record the registrar has to publish, which is what a secure-zone audit needs.
Turns DNSSEC on or off. Enabling it before the DS record is published, or leaving the DS record behind, is the failure this tool is gated for.
Disabling DNSSEC while the registrar still holds the DS record makes the whole domain fail to resolve (SERVFAIL), not just lose validation.
Every zone setting in one call: the audit a migration starts from. Cloudflare marks the operation deprecated but keeps serving it, and it is the only bulk read.
tools.note: Deprecated in the spec; the per-setting read below is the supported path.

tools.reason: Reads one setting by its documented id (ssl, min_tls_version, always_use_https, cache_level...).
Changes one setting. The supported way to turn on always_use_https or raise min_tls_version, one named value at a time.

Empties the edge cache for everything, by host, by tag, by URL or by prefix. Cloudflare flags it for confirmation because a full purge sends every request to the origin at once and cannot be recalled.
Lists the zone's IP allow/block rules, the state an incident responder reads first.
Blocks or challenges an IP, range, ASN or country at the edge: the first move against an abusive source.
Changes a rule's mode or target without deleting and recreating it, so the rule id stays stable for other systems.
Removes the block. Cloudflare marks it confirmation-worthy, so it is a reviewed note rather than a destructive flag: nothing is unrecoverable, the rule can be created again.
Lists the zone's lockdowns (host or path reachable only from stated IPs), the scheduled kind of access rule.
Closes a host or path to everyone outside a list of IPs, which is how a staging site or an admin path is protected.
Reads one lockdown, including the window it applies in.
Replaces a lockdown's urls, schedule and configuration. A mistaken replacement can open a path that was closed, which is why it stays behind the write gate.
Removes a lockdown, reopening the host or path to the internet. Cloudflare marks it confirmation-worthy; the write gate covers it.
Lists the user-agent block rules, the other half of the classic edge block list.
Blocks a user agent at the edge (a scraper, a bot that ignores robots.txt) without touching the origin.
Reads one user-agent rule by id.
Replaces a user-agent rule: the way to narrow a block that turned out to catch real traffic.
Removes a user-agent block. Cloudflare marks it confirmation-worthy; the write gate covers it and the rule can be recreated.
The account_id every account-scoped tool needs comes from here, and the legacy cloudflare adapter already ships this tool. Renamed from cloudflare_accounts_list_accounts to follow the naming rule.

tools.reason: Lists the user's API tokens with their status and expiry: the read that answers which credential this is and whether it is about to expire.

tools.reason: Reads one token, including the policies and resources it is scoped to.
tools.filterNote: Same x-fern-ignore group as the list above.

tools.reason: Validates the stored token and reports its status: the call that separates no token from a token Cloudflare rejects without spending a real request.
tools.filterNote: Same x-fern-ignore group; this is the call a credential check needs.

tools.reason: Lists the permission group ids a token policy is built from, which is how a caller discovers what a scope name means.
tools.filterNote: Same x-fern-ignore group; read-only and needed to interpret the token policies above.
